title: Event Merge Counts
prompt: A event report receives count objects from two sources. Write a function that returns one object with counts from matching keys added together.

explanation.beginner:
Example: eventMergeCounts({"open":2,"done":1}, {"open":3,"blocked":4}) produces {"open":5,"done":1,"blocked":4}. Copy the first collection of counts, then add each contribution from the next collection under the same key.

Compare “handles empty left objects”: input [{},{"a":1}] produces {"a":1}. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Copy the first collection of counts, then add each contribution from the next collection under the same key.

Tempting mistake: Replacing a count loses the earlier contribution; treating an absent count as undefined can produce NaN.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “handles empty left objects”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
